subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw expose a cross-channel Gateway receipt timestamp to agents, and what stable field name, timestamp format, and metadata block should carry it?
rationale: The absence is source-proven, but the fix creates a durable prompt/plugin SDK surface across channels, so automation should not choose the public contract unilaterally.

options.title: Add generic receipt timestamp
options.body: Expose one stable field such as `gatewayReceivedAt` and test propagation from receive context through SDK/channel ingress into agent-visible metadata.

options.title: Keep timing in diagnostics only
options.body: Use Gateway diagnostics or trace events for latency attribution without adding agent-visible prompt metadata.

options.title: Leave timing to channel plugins
options.body: Allow plugins to expose their own receipt timing, accepting inconsistent names and weaker cross-channel comparability.

recommendation.title: Add generic receipt timestamp
recommendation.body: Expose one stable field such as `gatewayReceivedAt` and test propagation from receive context through SDK/channel ingress into agent-visible metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history on the inbound envelope, plugin SDK helper, and metadata-contract surfaces that this decision would affect.
